---
title: "Header and footer links"
---

Configure links with Quarto's native navigation options. Askr supplies their
appearance, not a second link registry. The Header offers quick access; the
Footer keeps project, community and maintenance links available after reading.

## Native configuration

```yaml
website:
  navbar:
    tools-collapse: true
    tools:
      - icon: github
        href: https://github.com/your-organization/your-project
        text: GitHub repository
        aria-label: GitHub repository
  page-footer:
    left:
      - icon: github
        aria-label: GitHub repository
        href: https://github.com/your-organization/your-project
      - text: '<i class="bi bi-chat-dots" aria-hidden="true"></i> Community'
        href: https://community.example.org/
    center:
      - text: '<i class="bi bi-book" aria-hidden="true"></i> Maintenance guide'
        href: maintenance.qmd
      - text: '<i class="bi bi-people" aria-hidden="true"></i> Contributing'
        href: contributing.qmd
    right: "Your project's existing footer content"
```

Replace the example destinations with your own. GitHub appears twice because
these are two native navigation locations; Askr does not synchronize URLs.
Use [Bootstrap icon names](https://icons.getbootstrap.com/) and descriptive
`text` / `aria-label` values. Icon-only Footer links require `aria-label`:
Quarto attaches that name to their native icon. For unfamiliar community links,
a short visible label makes the purpose clearer.
Quarto 1.10.18's Footer text rendering replaces a sibling `icon` when both are
configured, so these examples put decorative Bootstrap icons inside native
`text` markup instead. `aria-hidden` leaves the visible label as the link name.

With `tools-collapse: true`, authored tools move into the
Areas panel when space is insufficient. Theme, Search and optional Logout stay
available in the Header. `false` keeps tools in the Header; use a small set so
they fit your narrowest viewport. Long Footer labels wrap rather than scroll.
Links use Quarto's native `href`, `target` and `rel` behavior; Askr does not force
new browser tabs. Existing links and build information remain authored content.

## Powered by Askr

The Footer's right section includes `Powered by Askr · version`. Askr links to
its documentation; the version links to its GitHub Release. The installed
extension's `_extension.yml` is the version authority, not `askr-versions.json`
or your document's package version. Unreleased local edits still show their
current package metadata version; this is not proof that those edits shipped.

To omit this credit:

```yaml
askr:
  footer:
    credit: false
```

Askr appends its credit without replacing your right-side content. Without
an authored Footer it creates a minimal credit-only Footer; with credit disabled
it creates nothing. No commit hash is generated or removed by Askr.

See [Quarto's navigation guide](https://quarto.org/docs/websites/website-navigation)
for menus, footer regions and additional native options.
